name: Skeinskitter
description: Stand beside the frame outside the arm's swing path and learn exactly where the arm will pass.

name: Steady Releasepin
description: Lift a shaped stone with a straight back and settle it into the sling cup without dropping it.

name: Winchgauge
description: Listen for the click of the pawl on each ratchet tooth to know the arm is held.

name: Armcuphit
description: Stand to one side and pull the release lanyard in one smooth motion to free the arm.

name: Measured Torsion
description: Drive wooden wedges under the wheels so the frame cannot roll back when the arm strikes its stop.

name: Warm Winchdrum
description: Repeat each crew call aloud so the whole crew hears that winder and loader and puller agree.

name: Light Throwarm
description: Walk a counted path from the stone pile to the cup so every load arrives in the same steps.

name: Smooth Skein
description: Two winders match their pace on the crank so the rope draws evenly without a jerk.

name: Folded Armcup
description: Shout the clear call and hold every hand back behind the frame line before the pull.

name: Judging Frameside
description: Sort stones by weight beside the frame so the loader never lifts one too heavy for the cup.

name: Judging Axlepin
description: Rotate tired hands off the crank on a fixed count so the crew keeps its strength through a long day.

name: Steady Basecradle
description: Set both hands on the crank handles with thumbs wrapped so the grip holds when the rope pulls hard.

name: Soft Axlepin
description: Brace the rear foot against a stake and wind with the legs and hips instead of the arms.

name: Even Skein
description: Watch each rope coil settle on the drum and stop winding when a coil rides over its neighbor.

name: Hooding Stoneload
description: Hold the crank at a half turn with the pawl dropped so the load rests on iron and not on hands.

name: Smooth Stoneload
description: Walk the crank back one tooth at a time while the pawl lifts so the arm lowers without a crash.

name: Armcupreview
description: Wipe fat along the drum axle between draws so the crank turns without squealing or sticking.

name: Short Bombardment
description: Chip a rough block into a rounded shot with short hammer blows that follow the grain.

name: Smooth Frameside
description: Heft each shaped stone twice and call its weight class so crews load matched shots in a row.

name: Deep Armcup
description: Carry a heavy stone against the hip with both arms underneath so the back never rounds.

name: Judging Basecradle
description: Step twice toward the cup and lower the stone into it in one motion without letting it roll.

name: Gentle Winchdrum
description: Run a hand along the cup rim to find a chipped edge that would foul the sling before loading.

name: Armcuphop
description: Roll a heavy stone up a short plank ramp beside the cup using a pole as a lever.

name: Arcflight Blow
description: Loose a plain stone from the cup to see whether it flies straight before real work begins.

name: Torsion Cowl
description: Drop the pawl into the tooth and tap it with a mallet to be sure it seats at full depth.

name: Watching Armcup
description: Read the worn teeth of the ratchet wheel with a thumbnail and mark any tooth that is rounding.

name: Kind Throwarm
description: Count each tooth aloud while unwinding with the pawl lifted so the load never runs free.

name: Soft Skein
description: Drive a fresh pin through the pawl arm with measured hammer strokes and test its swing.

name: Skeincowl
description: Stand a steady watch beside a wound catapult and keep the crew clear while the pawl holds the arm.

name: Throwarm Count
description: Breathe qi into the arms on each crank turn so the rope draws with less strain on the back.

name: Armcupgauge
description: Match one crank turn to one breath so qi and effort rise and fall together without waste.

name: Even Stoneload
description: Let the qi held in the winding arms drain away when the pawl drops so the muscles do not lock.

name: Skeinreview
description: Send a thread of qi along the rope to feel overtight fibers creak before they fray.

name: Raised Frameside
description: Press a qi-warmed palm on the frame beam to steady it against the shudder of a full draw.

name: Even Torsion
description: Touch the stone with qi and learn its weight and balance before it is set in the cup.

name: Skeinnote
description: Turn the loaded cup lip toward the target line so the stone leaves along the arm's path.

name: Winchdrum Note
description: Fold the sling pouch over the stone in thirds so it holds the shot until the arm lifts.

name: Winchnote
description: Shift the stone a finger's width back in the cup to stop it slipping out too soon.

name: Firm Ballistic
description: Time the release so the stone leaves the cup at the very top of the arm's rise.

name: Sharp Stonefall
description: Snap the lanyard with a flick of qi so the catch opens at the same instant on every pull.

name: Solid Axlepin
description: Pad the arm stop with rope bundles so the swing ends cleanly and the frame is spared.

name: Armcupnote
description: Guide the empty cup back down on the winch rope so it does not whip against the frame.

name: Winchreview
description: Drive a line of marked stakes along the target bearing and sight over them to aim the frame.

name: Steady Armcup
description: Stretch a cord from frame to target and read its angle before laying the bed to it.

name: Winchcount
description: Read a cloth flag on a pole to judge cross-wind and shift the aim a stake to match.

name: Firm Releasepin
description: Loose one plain stone and mark where it lands to set the distance of the next shot.

name: Deep Basecradle
description: Move the pawl one tooth up or down for each marked pace of error to correct a short shot.

name: Skeincount
description: Tilt the catapult bed with a wedge under the front to raise or lower the arc of the shot.

name: Skeingauge
description: Sweep the eye across the landing ground to find each impact mark and note it for the next shot.

name: Gnawing Unwind
description: Loose three stones in a counted rhythm on one setting to prove that the aim holds steady.

name: Deep Releasepin
description: Lay a plumb line along the bed to see whether the frame sits level on its ground.

name: Soft Throwarm
description: Pack earth and stones around the sleeper beams so the bed does not creep with each shot.

name: Solid Frameside
description: Wedge a rear strut against the frame to hold it down when the arm slams its stop.

name: Calm Releasepin
description: Tap each pin of the frame and listen for the dull note of a loosened joint.

name: Armcupcount
description: Press qi into a loose joint while driving its pin home so it seats and holds.

name: Stoneload Review
description: Step along the chosen ground and read its give underfoot before the wheels are set.

name: Smooth Winchdrum
description: Press a thumb into the twisted rope skein at three points to feel whether the twist is even.

name: Basecradle Review
description: Mark each skein bundle with the number of twists given so that both sides match.

name: Calm Skein
description: Work oil into the skein fibers with qi-warmed palms so they stay supple in damp weather.

name: Gentle Axlepin
description: Strike the tensioning peg and listen to the rope's note to judge how tight it is.

name: Gentle Basecradle
description: Turn the two tensioning pegs by equal turns so the arm sits true between the skeins.

name: Upward Torque
description: Cut away a frayed strand with a short knife stroke before it spreads through the bundle.

name: Axlepin Husk
description: Call the halt and step the crew back when a skein shows a slack side before any winding.
